definitions.explanation: Experiencing good luck or a fortunate outcome, often used as an exclamation when something unexpectedly good happens.

examples.japanese: ラッキー！{席|せき}が{空|あ}いてた。
examples.english: Lucky! There was an open seat.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}はラッキーな{日|ひ}だった。
{雨|あめ}の{予報|よほう}だったのに{晴|は}れて、ラッキーだった。
examples.english: Rain was forecast but it cleared up — I was lucky.

notes:
USAGE:
ラッキー is a casual, cheerful exclamation for small strokes of good luck. It is lighter and more informal than {幸運|こううん} (good fortune) or {運|うん}がいい (to be lucky). It is frequently used as a standalone exclamation: ラッキー！

The opposite is アンラッキー, though this is less commonly used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ラッキーな{日|ひ}: lucky day
- ラッキーだった: was lucky
- {超|ちょう}ラッキー: super lucky (casual intensifier)
